# sous

sous runs workflows in the background. A workflow is a JavaScript file of steps. A run is one
execution of it. A run goes on when this session ends, so the run's record is the truth and
your memory of it is not.

Treat a run like a subagent you started, with three differences. It outlives you. It can ask
the user. Its work lands on a git branch for review.

## Start here

Run `sous status --json`. It says what needs the user, what runs and what finished.
Every reply has `next`, the exact calls you can make now. Use them as written. A call may hold
a placeholder such as `<red|blue>` or `"<note>"`. Fill it in, and keep the rest.
For the rest, run `sous guide`.

## Start a run

1. `sous workflows --json` lists the workflows and their inputs.
2. `sous run <name> --<input> <value> --json` starts it and returns at once.
3. Tell the user the run id, what it will do, what it may ask, and what the last runs cost.

Do not start a workflow marked `startedBy: "people"`. Give the user the `sous run` command to
type. Never try to get around it.

## Wait for it

In Claude Code, run `sous wait <run> --json` as a background command. You are called
when it returns. Elsewhere, run `sous wait <run> --timeout 540 --json`, and call it again
while it exits 5. Never wait with sleep or a loop of `sous show`.
If the user wants a running step to change course, use `sous tell`. Stop a step only to redo
it. See `sous guide steer`.

The exit code says why: 0 completed, 1 failed, 2 paused, 3 stopped, 4 asks.

## When it asks

A question with `answeredBy: "people"` is the user's. Show it in full, with its choices.
Pass their words on with the call in `next`. If the user is not there, say that the run
waits for them as long as it takes, and stop. Never answer it with a choice you made.
Only a question with `answeredBy: "anyone"` is yours to answer.

## When it ends

Completed means the script ended, not that the work is right. Read `result`, `review` and
the diff on the run's branch. Report the outcome, the branch,
what you checked and what you did not. Never merge, push or discard unless asked.

## When it pauses or fails

Read `pauseReason`, `failure` and `next`. `sous step <run> <label> --json` shows what the
failed step did. `sous resume` runs the failed step again and keeps the finished ones.
`sous rerun` pays for every step again, so ask first.
A run paused at the usage limit resumes by itself.

## Write or change a workflow

Before you change or run an unknown workflow, read `sous workflows show <name> --json`.
To write one, read `sous guide writing` first. It says where to save. Show the user what you
will save, and save only after their yes. Run `sous check <name> --dry-run --json` until it
passes. Add a schedule, save into `~/.sous/workflows/`, or change who may start a workflow only
when the user asked.

sous starts a new or changed workflow only after the user approves its text. Show them the
diff since their last yes, `sous workflows show <name> --diff --json`. When they agree, run
`sous workflows approve <name> --by person --json`, or they type `sous workflows approve <name>`.
A yes to the whole text you saved unchanged counts. Never approve without their yes.

## Errors

A refusal has `error.change`, what to change, and `error.call`, the call to make instead.
Make that call, not the refused one. When `call` is null, read `change`. If it needs
the user, tell them.

## Inside a run

If `SOUS_RUN_ID` is set, you are a step of that run. You may start workflows that allow it.
Leave the inbox, the other runs and the workflow files alone.

# Write or change a workflow

Write or change a workflow only with the person's yes. Show them what you will save, and save
only after they agree. Save in the project's `.sous/workflows/<name>.js`. Change
`~/.sous/workflows/`, a schedule, or `startedBy` only when the person asked for that.

Start from a workflow that exists. `sous workflows --json` lists them. Before you change or run
one you don't know, read `sous workflows show <name> --json`: its steps, inputs, approval and
last runs. `sous agents --json` lists the agents a step can name.

## The person approves it

sous keeps the person's yes for each workflow's exact text. A new or changed workflow does not
start from an agent, a step of a run or a schedule until the person approves it. A scheduled run of
it is skipped, and the person gets a notice. Once you saved it and the check passes, show them
`sous workflows show <name> --diff --json`, what changed since their last yes. Tell them sous
starts it from you, a run or a schedule only after they approve it, by saying yes to you or with
`sous workflows approve <name>` in their own terminal.

When they say yes to you, run `sous workflows approve <name> --by person --json`. A yes they gave
to the whole text you showed them counts, if you saved that text unchanged. If the check made you
change it, show them the diff and ask again. Without
`--by person` an agent's approve is refused with `needs_person`. Never approve without their yes.
A person's own `sous run <name>` approves the text it runs. Never edit, move or delete
`approvals.json` or `approved/` in sous's home. Without them no workflow counts as approved.

## The file

```js
export const meta = {
  name: "ticket",
  description: "Implement a ticket, review it",
  inputs: {
    ticket: { type: "string", description: "What to build", required: true },
    rounds: { type: "number", default: 3 },
  },
  outputs: { summary: "What was built" },
  place: "worktree",
  startedBy: "anyone",
  timeout: "2h",
}

const built = await agent(`Implement this ticket:\n${args.ticket}`, { agentType: "implementer", label: "implementer", keepSession: true })
const review = await agent(`Review the change for: ${args.ticket}`, { agentType: "reviewer", label: "reviewer" })
await agent(`Address this review:\n${review}`, { continue: "implementer" })
return { summary: built }
```

- `meta` needs `name` and `description`. `inputs` become flags of `sous run`.
- Give every step a `label`. Resume matches steps by prompt, options and label.
- `Math.random()`, `Date.now()` and `new Date()` with no argument throw. A resume replays the
  script and must take the same path. Pass a time or a random value as an input.
- Cap each loop, usually with an input such as `rounds`.

## Steps

- `agent(prompt, options)` runs one agent. Options include `label`, `agentType`, `model`,
  `schema`, `timeout`, `skills`, `mcp`, `keepSession`, `continue` and `ask`.
- `sh`, `js`, `py`, `run` and `waitUntil` run code on this machine and spend no tokens.
- `ask(question, { choices })` and `checkpoint(prompt, { kind, choices })` ask the person.
  `answeredBy: "anyone"` in `ask` lets an agent answer too. `agent()` with `ask: true` takes it.
- `breakpoint(title, step)` runs the step, then waits for the person to approve it. It is always
  for people, so it takes no `answeredBy`.
- `parallel`, `pipeline`, `retry`, `gate`, `choose` and `workflow` shape the flow.

## Check it

```sh
sous check ticket --ticket "x" --json
sous check ticket --ticket "x" --dry-run --json
sous check ticket --ticket "x" --dry-run --answers answers.json --json
```

The check parses the script, fits the inputs, and finds each agent, workflow and MCP server. A
dry run runs the workflow once with stand-in agents. It spends no tokens. Code steps run for real
in a copy, so a step that writes to `SOUS_PROJECT` still changes the project. `--answers` gives
the stand-ins' answers by step label, such as `{"reviewer *": {"approved": true}}`.

Fix what the check reports until it passes, then show the person the file and the result.
